brief: A small single-storey false-front clapboard shop painted green with white trim, a gable roof behind the square front, a display window and door. One photo. Older than 1970: Petoskey's Gaslight District (the town's model) is a row of 1880-1910 brick commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Hosman & Wheeler meat market (Petoskey MI, c.1900): a small frame false-front shop -- a square front with a bracketed cornice hiding a gable roof -- painted green, a big multi-pane shop window; now a heritage centre (sign); a fire hydrant

why.note: the frontier false front: a square parapet makes a cheap gabled shed look like a 'real' store
